card.name: Maruni
card.tagline: One of the oldest Nepali/Gorkha festival dances
card.profile: Maruni is one of the oldest and most popular Nepali (Gorkha) folk dances, practised in Nepal and among Nepali-speaking communities of Darjeeling, Sikkim, Assam, Bhutan and Myanmar, performed especially during Tihar and Dashain (Wikipedia). Its choreographic origin is traditionally linked to the army of King Balihang (14th century); dancers wear colourful clothes, rich ornaments and nose rings, accompanied by the nine-instrument Naumati Baja, with the madal (maadal) drum predominating (Wikipedia; Farsight Nepal). The troupe characteristically includes a male jester/prankster figure called the 'Dhatu Waray' who provides comic relief; variants include Maruni, Thale Maruni and Sorathi (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Historically danced by men (including male performers cross-dressing as women), Maruni functions as a communal festival dance that knits together Nepali-Gorkha identity across the eastern Himalaya, sustained today by community and diaspora performance (Farsight Nepal; Darjeeling History Club).
card.image_significance: The oldest Nepali festive dance. A representative image shows ornate costume and expressive hand-gesture (mudra) detail — Nepali community, India/Nepal.
